questions.q: Why does self-attention need positional encoding added to the input at all?
options: Because nn.MultiheadAttention requires a fixed-size input
Because self-attention is permutation-equivariant -- it computes relevance from content alone and has no inherent notion of token order
Because PyTorch's softmax function requires sorted input
Because positional encoding reduces the number of parameters needed
questions.explain: Without positional information, shuffling the input tokens would shuffle the outputs correspondingly with no change in the relationships computed -- attention alone carries no sense of order.

questions.q: How is positional encoding combined with the token embedding in both the sinusoidal and learned approaches?
options: Concatenated, doubling the embedding dimension
Added elementwise, keeping the same embedding dimension
Multiplied elementwise
It replaces the token embedding entirely
questions.explain: Both sinusoidal and learned positional encodings are added elementwise to the token embedding, so d_model stays unchanged.

questions.q: What is a key practical difference between sinusoidal and learned positional encodings?
options: Sinusoidal encodings require a GPU; learned ones do not
Sinusoidal encoding is a fixed formula that can in principle extend beyond the trained sequence length; learned embeddings are a lookup table fixed to max_seq_len positions
Learned embeddings can only be used with CNNs
There is no practical difference
questions.explain: Sinusoidal positional encoding is computed from a formula and isn't tied to a specific maximum length, while a learned nn.Embedding table only has entries for positions up to max_seq_len.

questions.q: In the sinusoidal formula, what varies across the different dimension pairs of the positional encoding vector for a single position?
options: Nothing -- every dimension pair is identical
The frequency of the sine/cosine wave, which differs across dimension pairs
The batch size
The vocabulary size
questions.explain: Each pair of dimensions (sin, cos) oscillates at a different frequency determined by 10000^(2i/d_model), giving each position a unique, structured encoding.

questions.q: Why didn't RNNs need an explicit positional encoding mechanism?
options: RNNs process sequences of a fixed, known length only
Order was already baked into the recurrence itself, since each hidden state is computed in strict sequence from the previous one
RNNs don't use embeddings at all
RNNs apply positional encoding automatically inside nn.RNN
questions.explain: An RNN's step-by-step recurrence inherently processes tokens in order, so position is implicitly encoded in when each hidden state update happens.
